This isn't an authentic curry by any means, but everything needs a name.

Should feed 3-4

  • 1 lb chicken thighs (with skin)
  • 1 onion, chopped
  • 4 cloves garlic
  • dried ancho chiles
  • turmeric
  • salt and pepper
  • 3 cups uncooked basmati rice

Cook the rice how you normally would for plain white rice. I have a magic Japanese robot that makes it for me....

Get your cast iron skillet ready!

Cut the bones out of the thighs. Cut them into small pieces and put into skillet on medium. The fat in the skin will provide enough fat to cook with.

Add the chopped onion.

Season with salt and pepper to taste. Try 2 teaspoons of each, if you have no idea.

Add enough turmeric to make everything a deep yellow. As long as there isn't so much it gets crunchy, you're ok. Maybe 3-4 teaspoons.Take the dried ancho chiles. How many? Maybe four around the size of your palm. Remove the stems, but I like leaving in the seeds. Ancho aren't spicy, but have a rich fruity flavor.

Grind these puppies up in a coffee grinder. I have a coffee grinder I only use for these. Makes a lovely dark powder.

Make sure it's totally a powder, then add it to the chicken.

At this point, just let everything sautee. Keep stirring periodically and doing with your spatula. As the chicken cooks through it'll become easy to break apart. It ends up becoming shredded.

You should have everything on a medium heat, do nothing should go wrong very quickly. Just keep checking in and chopping, scraping the bottom of the pan, and watching the onions turn brown.

To check the chicken, chop open any large chunks and make sure everything is white all the way through. When the chicken looks done, crush the cloves of garlic into the dish and stir it around. Let it cook for a couple more minutes, then serve on the white rice!

Notes:

Gotta use skin-on chicken. Gives you the fat to cook with, fat-soluble nutrients, and tiny bits of crispy skin.

When sauteeing onions, you want to draw out the moisture. Salt does this, so try to season the chicken and onion both with salt.

This is definitely a dish that benefits from cooking longer on moderate heat. The longer you go, the more caramelized the onions get, the more the flavors meld. As long as you don't use too high a heat you shouldn't dry out the chicken and everything will be nice and tasty.

This dish saves well in the fridge. Just put the rice and chicken in the same container. When you reheat it, put it into a pot and stir it around for 5-10 min. The fat in the chicken helps you reheat the rice, too. Just mix it all around in there.

Again, I crush the garlic and add it at the end for a strong garlic flavor. If you cook it longer, or mince instead of crushing, its milder. Cooking longer also gives it a sweetness.

Enjoy!
